objective: Audit capability graph completeness — each meaningful capability attributable to source/capability/test surface/evidence/certification.

findings.entity: 14 CLI routes without catalog metadata entry
findings.impact: These routes are not represented in the capability graph, so blast-radius → capability → execution chains may not recognize them. Under M46.5 (workflow truth) and M46.18 (command consolidation), each must either be registered or deprecated.
Two distinct implementations of the same capability. One must be deprecated per Rule 1.6.
These are valid latent capabilities from prior C47-C50 milestones. They are intentionally latent (not on the default workflow). Decision: keep latent; document ownership.

findings.details: Many evidence kinds (latent_capability_audit, strengthening_proposal, diagnostic_report, lint_report, test_pass, forensic_report, evidence_invalidations, bypass_risk_analysis, typecheck_report, knowledge_report, reconciliation_report, configuration_authority_report, certification_report, format_report, capability_graph) are produced but never programmatically consumed.
findings.impact: External consumers (CI, human review) are expected. This is acceptable but indicates the control plane reads evidence manually — partially defeating the automation goal. M46.19 (Evidence Unification) will document explicit consumer chains.

capability_to_production_attribution.production_attribution_gap: Each capability node maps to a verify.py command, but most are not directly attributable to a production capability (e.g., engines). The capability graph is mostly about the verification system itself, not the system-under-test.
capability_to_production_attribution.production_capabilities_discovered: Engine capabilities are listed in CAPABILITY_AUDIT.md and CAPABILITY_COVERAGE.md at repo root (15K + 5K bytes). Those were not merged into the runtime capability graph.
